as_told.title: Malmgren in the Cuban Missile Crisis war room confronts Curtis LeMay

plain: During the Cuban missile crisis of 1962, a young aide named Harold Malmgren, then about 26 or 27, says he was sent by President John F. Kennedy into "the tank," the Pentagon's secure meeting room for the top generals, to stall Curtis LeMay, the Air Force's commanding general, who was pressing for a nuclear strike. Malmgren, later a presidential adviser, tells Michels himself that he argued it was madness, because "if you hit Moscow, there's no one to talk to," and he names Defense Secretary Robert McNamara and the White House adviser McGeorge Bundy as being there. A commentator named Matthew Pines, who relays what Malmgren told him, tells it twice on the show, once as Kennedy telling Malmgren to "stall him out" and once just as holding LeMay back from possibly launching nuclear weapons.
